_readme: Nights that never fall below 20 C, and days above each city's own extreme-heat thresholds, per European city, each against its own record. One thermometer per city, nights and days from the same rows of the same record. City warming included. Not a climate measurement and never presented as one.

definition.name: Tropical night
definition.rule: daily minimum temperature at or above 20.0 C
definition.standard: ETCCDI index TR, as published by European met services. Not a threshold we chose.

day_definition.rule: daily maximum at or above this station's own 90th, 95th and 99th percentile of July-August maxima, 1971-2000
day_definition.standard_es: AEMET's own published rule. Verified by reproducing their published Madrid 36.4 C and Seville 41.2 C exactly.
day_definition.standard_fr: THE SAME METHOD, NOT A PUBLISHED FRENCH RULE. Meteo-France publishes no percentile equivalent, so the French thresholds are our application of AEMET's method to French stations. Defensible, and NOT the same evidential standing. The phrase 'AEMET's own rule, not ours' must not be copied across.
day_definition.why_not_35c: A flat 35 C is not a standard and is not usable across cities: measured 2011-2025 it gives 0.5 days a year in Barcelona and 66.8 in Seville.

lead.claim: Not one of these cities is having an ordinary summer for hot nights.

headline.may_not_say: 2026 is NOT the worst year on this measure. 2003 produced 12 on the same to-date basis and is inside living memory for this readership.
headline.the_better_story: Three of the four worst years on this measure are the last four years. A pattern rather than an event.
headline.fragile_note: A record held by a single night. Carries its margin rather than hiding it.
headline.caveat: 2026 is counted to 2-3 August with the season unfinished. Prior years are counted to the same date, so the comparison is like-for-like today, but 2026 can still add records before September.

day_headline.measure: days at or above this city's own 95th percentile of July-August maxima, counted to the same cut
day_headline.may_say_worst_note: 2026 sets more city day-records than any year in the window, including 2003. This is the OPPOSITE of the nights constraint, where 2003 remains worse and `may_not_say` applies. The two instruments do not share a caveat.

cities_without_day_multiple_note: These stations opened after 1961, so their 1961-1990 baseline is part-length and drawn from the warmer end of the period. The multiple is NOT EMITTED rather than flagged, so it cannot be rendered or reinstated. Their recent rate stands on a complete window and is emitted.

Madrid.date_note: counted_to is the cut every year in the series is measured to. last_observation is how far the source now reaches. Advancing the cut is a substantive change, not a refresh.

rank.tie_note: A TIE IS NOT A RECORD. rank counts prior years at or above 2026, so a tied year keeps 2026 off first place. Recomputing with a strict greater-than gives a different and more alarming answer; do not recompute.
rank.requires_series_note: This rank may not be rendered without the series below it. A bare rank is an alarm; the same rank beside its ordinary years is a calibrated statement.

series_to_same_date.cut_note: Every year counted to this calendar day. NOT comparable to a figure cut at a different day, and cities from different countries have different cuts because the publication lag differs, so a cross-city ranking cannot use a single one.
series_to_same_date.due_note: Equal to expected_slots: an annual series, every prior year already due.
series_to_same_date.slot_basis: Span of the station record as held by the published source. Taken BEFORE any completeness filter and never from the emitted series.
series_to_same_date.unusable_note: Observed and computed, but below the completeness bar of 90% of days from 1 May to the cut. OBSERVED BUT NOT USABLE, which is not absent. Must not be drawn as a gap.
series_to_same_date.gap_note: Slots with no record at all. This is the one to draw.

days.threshold_basis: 90th/95th/99th percentile of this station's own July-August daily maxima, 1971-2000.

Madrid.full_year_series_note: Counted over whole years, so its completeness bar is stricter than the to-date series and it holds fewer years. The two are not interchangeable and must not share an axis.

sources_note: Every published figure comes from a national met service that permits commercial reuse. ECA&D is not read anywhere in this pipeline.
coverage_note: Spain and France. The night metric does not work in northern Europe, where tropical nights are near zero and ratios divide by almost nothing.
